steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
Here’s a high-level, conceptual walkthrough of how a Transformer works:  

1. Input Representation  
   • Tokens → Embeddings: each input token (word, subword, etc.) is mapped to a continuous vector.  
   • Positional Encoding: since there’s no recurrence, we add a position-specific signal so the model knows token order.  

2. Self-Attention Mechanism  
   • Queries, Keys, Values: from each token embedding we compute three vectors—q, k, v—via learned linear projections.  
   • Scaled Dot-Product Attention: for each query qᵢ we measure its compatibility with all keys kⱼ by qᵢ·kⱼ/√d, apply softmax to get weights, then take a weighted sum of the values v.  
   • Intuition: every token “looks at” all other tokens and gathers context in a single pass.  

3. Multi-Head Attention  
   • Multiple Attention Heads: we split embeddings into subspaces and run several attention computations in parallel.  
   • Why? Different heads can learn to focus on different kinds of relationships (syntax, long-range dependencies, etc.).  
   • The outputs are concatenated and linearly projected back to the original dimension.  

4. Feed-Forward Network (FFN)  
   • Position-wise Dense Layers: each position passes independently through a small MLP (usually two linear layers with a nonlinearity between).  
   • Purpose: introduce nonlinearity and mix the information captured by attention.  

5. Residual Connections & Layer Normalization  
   • Each sub-layer (attention or FFN) is wrapped in “Add & Norm”: you add its input (residual) to its output and then normalize.  
   • This stabilizes training and lets gradients flow more easily.  

6. Stacking Layers  
   • You repeat (Multi-Head Attention → Add & Norm → FFN → Add & Norm) multiple times to build deep representations.  

7. Encoder-Decoder Structure (for tasks like translation)  
   • Encoder: a stack of self-attention + FFN layers processes the source.  
   • Decoder: similarly stacked, but each layer has two attention steps—masked self-attention (to prevent seeing future tokens) and encoder-decoder attention (to attend to encoder outputs).  

8. Final Output  
   • For classification/sequencing tasks, you take the topmost layer’s representations and project them to your target vocabulary (or label space), often using softmax to produce probabilities.  

Key advantages  
   • Parallelism: unlike RNNs, all tokens are processed simultaneously.  
   • Long-Range Dependency: self-attention directly connects any two positions, making it easier to capture distant relationships.  
   • Scalability: stacking attention and FFN blocks builds very deep, expressive models.
